---
title: "Fighter Style Clustering"
output: html_document
---

This report prepares fighter career statistics, runs reduced K-means clustering, and saves one cluster label for each fighter.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}


library(clustrd)

set.seed(123)

# Find the folder containing this R Markdown file.
# This makes relative paths work whether the file is knitted or run manually.
rmd_path <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)

if (is.null(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
  rmd_dir <- if (dir.exists(file.path(getwd(), "styles"))) {
    file.path(getwd(), "styles")
  } else {
    getwd()
  }
} else {
  rmd_dir <- dirname(normalizePath(rmd_path, mustWork = TRUE))
}

# Evaluate later chunks from the R Markdown file's folder.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = rmd_dir)

data_path <- file.path("..", "data_clean", "fighter_career_stats.csv")
output_path <- "clusters3_redo.csv"

if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find data_clean/fighter_career_stats.csv")
}
```

## Load the data

This block reads the fighter-level dataset and separates fighter names from the variables used for clustering.

```{r load-data}
fighter_data <- read.csv(
  data_path,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

fighter_names <- fighter_data$fighter

# Use columns 3 through 56 as the clustering variables.
# The first two columns are the fighter name and total fight count.
cluster_data <- fighter_data[, 3:56, drop = FALSE]

cat("Fighters:", nrow(cluster_data), "\n")
cat("Clustering variables:", ncol(cluster_data), "\n")
```

## Prepare the clustering variables

This block checks for missing values and replaces them with the mean of their respective variable. The optional TD_def switch allows that variable to be removed instead.

```{r prepare-data}
missing_before <- colSums(is.na(cluster_data))
missing_before[missing_before > 0]

# Keep FALSE for mean imputation.
# Change to TRUE to remove TD_def before clustering.
remove_td_def <- FALSE

if (remove_td_def && "TD_def" %in% names(cluster_data)) {
  cluster_data$TD_def <- NULL
}

# Replace each missing value with that variable's observed mean.
for (column_name in names(cluster_data)) {
  column_mean <- mean(cluster_data[[column_name]], na.rm = TRUE)

  if (is.nan(column_mean)) {
    stop(sprintf("Cannot impute %s because it has no observed values.", column_name))
  }

  missing_values <- is.na(cluster_data[[column_name]])
  cluster_data[[column_name]][missing_values] <- column_mean
}

stopifnot(!anyNA(cluster_data))

cat("Variables used:", ncol(cluster_data), "\n")
cat("Missing values remaining:", sum(is.na(cluster_data)), "\n")
```

## Fit the clustering model

This block runs reduced K-means. The variables are centered and scaled so that variables with larger numeric units do not dominate the analysis.

```{r reduced-k-means}
rkm_fit <- clustrd::cluspca(
  data = cluster_data,
  nclus = 3,
  ndim = 6,
  method = "RKM",
  center = TRUE,
  scale = TRUE,
  nstart = 100,
  seed = 123
)

summary(rkm_fit)
```

## Save cluster labels

This block attaches the cluster assignment to each fighter and writes the result to a CSV file.

```{r export-clusters}
cluster_labels <- as.integer(rkm_fit$cluster)

clusters3_redo <- data.frame(
  fighter = fighter_names,
  cluster = cluster_labels
)

write.csv(
  clusters3_redo,
  file = output_path,
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Saved:", normalizePath(output_path, mustWork = FALSE), "\n")
print(table(clusters3_redo$cluster))
head(clusters3_redo)
```

## Summarize cluster profiles

This final block calculates the average value of every clustering variable within each cluster. It helps describe how the clusters differ.

```{r cluster-profile}
cluster_profile <- aggregate(
  cluster_data,
  by = list(cluster = clusters3_redo$cluster),
  FUN = mean
)

cluster_profile
```

## Run Comparison of hyperparameters

Testing out the different values for clusters and reduced dimensions, to see how silhouette score changes. 

```{r}
library(cluster)
library(mclust)

nclus = 3:6
ndim = 4:7

evaluate_rkm <- function(nclus, ndim) {
  fit <- clustrd::cluspca(
    data = cluster_data,
    nclus = nclus,
    ndim = ndim,
    method = "RKM",
    center = TRUE,
    scale = TRUE,
    nstart = 100,
    seed = 123
  )

  labels <- as.integer(fit$cluster)
  coordinates <- as.matrix(fit$obscoord)

  silhouette_score <- mean(
    cluster::silhouette(labels, dist(coordinates))[, "sil_width"]
  )

  cluster_sizes <- table(labels)

  list(
    fit = fit,
    labels = labels,
    silhouette = silhouette_score,
    cluster_sizes = cluster_sizes
  )
}


# Create every nclus/ndim combination.
settings <- expand.grid(
  nclus = 3:6,
  ndim = 4:7
)

models <- vector("list", nrow(settings))
results <- vector("list", nrow(settings))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(settings))) {
  current_nclus <- settings$nclus[i]
  current_ndim <- settings$ndim[i]

  evaluation <- evaluate_rkm(
    nclus = current_nclus,
    ndim = current_ndim
  )

  models[[i]] <- evaluation$fit

  sizes <- evaluation$cluster_sizes

  results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    nclus = current_nclus,
    ndim = current_ndim,
    silhouette_score = evaluation$silhouette,
    cluster_sizes = paste(
      paste0("Cluster ", names(sizes), " = ", as.integer(sizes)),
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}

# Combine all results and rank them by silhouette score.
results_table <- do.call(rbind, results)
results_table <- results_table[
  order(-results_table$silhouette_score),
]

rownames(results_table) <- NULL
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(
  results_table,
  aes(
    x = factor(ndim),
    y = factor(nclus),
    fill = silhouette_score
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", silhouette_score)),
    color = "black",
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "C",
    name = "Silhouette\nscore"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "RKM Silhouette Scores",
    subtitle = "Comparison across cluster counts and reduced dimensions",
    x = "Number of reduced dimensions",
    y = "Number of clusters"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

best_result <- results_table[which.max(results_table$silhouette_score), ]

best_result
```
